question.problem:
According to the Chinese remainder theorem, which of the following systems of congruences has a unique solution modulo $144?$ 

$$
\text{I.}\,\{\begin{aligned}x≡1 & (\text{mod}\,3) \\ x≡4 & (\text{mod}\,6) \\ x≡7 & (\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}\,\text{II.}\,\{\begin{aligned}x≡3 & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ x≡8 & (\text{mod}\,16)\end{aligned}\,\text{III.}\,\{\begin{aligned}x≡5 & (\text{mod}\,6) \\ x≡7 & (\text{mod}\,24)\end{aligned}\,
$$
question.worked_solution:
The Chinese remainder theorem states that if the natural numbers ${n}_{1},{n}_{2},…,{n}_{k}$ are pairwise coprime, meaning that $\text{gcd}({n}_{i},{n}_{j})=1$ whenever $i\ne j,$ then for any integers ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},…,{a}_{k}$ the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x≡{a}_{1} & (\text{mod}\,{n}_{1}) \\ x≡{a}_{2} & (\text{mod}\,{n}_{2}) \\ \,⋮ \\ x≡{a}_{k} & (\text{mod}\,{n}_{k})\end{aligned}
$$

has a unique solution modulo ${n}_{1}{n}_{2}⋯{n}_{k}.$

Let's now inspect each of the given systems in turn.

- The theorem does *not* apply to system I since $3$ and $6$ are not coprime: 

$$
\text{gcd}(3,6)=3>1
$$

- The theorem applies to system II. The numbers $9$ and $16$ are pairwise coprime natural numbers. Therefore, according to the Chinese remainder theorem, the system has a unique solution modulo $9\cdot 16=144.$

- The theorem does *not* apply to system III since $6$ and $24$ are not coprime: 

$$
\text{gcd}(6,24)=6>1
$$

So, the correct answer is "II only."
